authoritative_for: Krisis owns completed-exchange observation, binary classification, deterministic full-conversation document construction, target-bound outbox delivery and Annals acceptance receipts.
The migration-compatible Krisis SQLite projection is authoritative for those operational records and retains retired Decisions history without making Krisis a decision library.
not_authoritative_for: The cited user message supplies decision authority.
Conversations owns normalized conversation resolution, Nucleus owns bounded execution evidence, and Annals owns the accepted decision library and its search and retrieval behavior.

covers: All supported public Krisis capture outcomes, installation and recovery operations, and development operations in this release.
excludes: Help and version display, implementation primitives, direct SQLite access, retired digest and review operations, upstream product capabilities, current runtime readiness, and downstream Annals behavior are outside this inventory claim.

shared_access_and_trust: Krisis interfaces run locally for the current user. Each entry declares its reads, writes, and calls to other products.
Catalog presence does not authorize deployment, live state changes, direct database access, or interpretation of model output as decision authority.
shared_privacy_and_retention: Private local state retains frozen normalized conversation, exact Nucleus requests/results, and pending document bytes.
After matching Annals acceptance, Krisis clears its outbox body but keeps the private document run and delivery receipt. Nucleus and Annals own their separate retention.
compatibility_and_retirement: Provider release identifies bundle bytes. Entry contracts, SQLite schema 5, document tool schemas and downstream exchange contracts have independent versions.
Retired Decisions state remains migration-decodable and its lifecycle stream remains read-only for existing consumers; digest, review, email, and daily scheduling are disabled.
operational_limits: Observation is serial. Full encoded prompts are at most 262144 UTF-8 bytes and are never truncated. Positive summaries contain at most 1000 Unicode scalar values.
No availability, latency, throughput, output, or retention service-level objective is promised.
